title: Cap. VI Arg. 12: true election decree segregates singular persons
pass_a_gloss: The true decree of election is segregative of singular persons, whom God, others being passed by, from special mercy has infallibly destined to the obtaining of salvation. The very word of electing proves this, under whose formal signification is indicated the acceptance of one, the other being rejected. But in that decree of Arminian election, Whosoever shall have believed shall obtain eternal life; Whosoever shall have remained unbelieving shall perish, there is no segregation of singular persons from others, no passing by or rejection of others, since by such a decree God promises salvation equally to any man, and threatens perdition equally to any.
pass_b_english: The true election decree segregates singular persons — those God, others passed by, has from special mercy infallibly destined to obtain salvation. The very word elect proves it: under its formal sense one is accepted, the other rejected. But in that Arminian decree — Whoever believes shall obtain eternal life; whoever remains unbelieving shall perish — there is no segregation of singular persons, no passing by or rejection of others, since by it God promises salvation equally to anyone and threatens perdition equally to anyone.
source_text: Verum decretum electionis est segregativum singularium personarum, quos Deus aliis praeteritis ex speciali misericordia ad salutem obtinendam infallibiliter destinavit. Ipsum vocabulum eligendi hoc arguit, sub cujus formali significatione indicatur acceptio unius, altero rejecto. At in illo Arminianae electionis decreto, Quicunque crediderit, vitam aeternam obtinebit; Quicunque incredulus manserit, peribit, nulla est singularium personarum segregatio ab aliis, nulla aliarum praeteritio aut rejectio, cum Deus tali decreto cuilibet homini ex aequo salutem polliceatur, cuilibet ex aequo perditionem interminetur.
